title: Base change for a general morphism reduces to the proper part
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, and put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with a chosen compactification $X\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be any scheme morphism and form the Cartesian base changes [def-pc-fibre-product]
$$
\overline X'=\overline X\times_Y Y',\qquad X'=X\times_Y Y',\qquad
X'\xrightarrow{j_0'}\overline X'\xrightarrow{p'}Y',
$$
with projections $\overline g:\overline X'\to\overline X$ and $g':X'\to X$, and $f'=p'j_0'$. Work with constant $A$-module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites and their ordinary unbounded derived categories and operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Suppose the chosen compactifications of $f$ and $f'$ carry ambient exceptional right adjoint data [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], taken over the respective scheme bases $Y$ and $Y'$. Write $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_{0!}$ and $Rf'_!^{c'}=Rp'_*j'_{0!}$ for the chosen compactification functors and $Rf^\times,Rf'^\times$ for their supplied right adjoints. Also specify the proper adjunctions $Rp_*\dashv Rp^\times$ and $Rp'_*\dashv Rp'^\times$ involved in the proper comparison.

The comparisons are specified as follows, using the mate bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Let
$$\delta_p:Rp'_*L\overline g^*\longrightarrow Lg^*Rp_*$$
be the reverse direct-image comparison whose mate is the proper comparison
$$\beta_p:L\overline g^*Rp^\times\longrightarrow Rp'^\times Lg^*.$$
Equivalently, specifying $\beta_p$ specifies $\delta_p$ by the inverse mate bijection; no invertibility of $\delta_p$ is assumed. Let
$$\alpha:Lg'^*Lj_0^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lj_0'^*L\overline g^*$$
be the canonical pullback-composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Let $\gamma:j'_{0!}Lg'^*\to L\overline g^*j_{0!}$ be its inverse mate for the open adjunctions $j_{0!}\dashv Lj_0^*$ and $j'_{0!}\dashv Lj_0'^*$ [prop-exc-open-adjoint]. Define $\beta_f:Lg'^*Rf^\times\to Rf'^\times Lg^*$ to be the mate, for the supplied compact-support adjunctions, of
$$
\delta_f:Rp'_*j'_{0!}Lg'^*
\xrightarrow{Rp'_*\gamma}Rp'_*L\overline g^*j_{0!}
\xrightarrow{\delta_pj_{0!}}Lg^*Rp_*j_{0!}.
$$
Thus these are the adjunction comparisons for the proper square and its paste with the open square, with their maps fixed rather than merely unspecified natural transformations. If $\beta_p$ is an isomorphism, then $\beta_f$ is an isomorphism. This is a conditional statement about the supplied ambient adjunctions, with no unconditional ambient-datum assertion.

proof.text:
By [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], the chosen left adjoints are $F=Rp_*j_{0!}$ and $F'=Rp'_*j'_{0!}$; this formula is stated over a scheme base, so it applies with bases $Y$ and $Y'$ even when $g$ is arbitrary. For $j_0$, [prop-exc-open-adjoint] supplies $j_{0!}\dashv Lj_0^*$; compose it with the supplied $Rp_*\dashv Rp^\times$. For $j_0'$, the same cited statement, applied to that open immersion and the same finite ring $A$, supplies $j'_{0!}\dashv Lj_0'^*$; compose it with $Rp'_*\dashv Rp'^\times$. The theorem [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] gives canonical isomorphisms
$$\rho:Rf^\times\xrightarrow{\sim}Lj_0^*Rp^\times,\qquad
\rho':Rf'^\times\xrightarrow{\sim}Lj_0'^*Rp'^\times.$$
Its unit/counit clause says these identifications preserve the supplied adjunctions, which is needed when comparing their mates.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: compact-support factorization and uniqueness of right adjoints

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] to $(h,k)=(g',j_0)$ and $(h,k)=(j_0',\overline g)$, with the constant coefficient sheaves $A$ and their canonical inverse-image identifications. These identifications are the finite constant-coefficient ones of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; both composite coefficient maps send a constant $a$ to the same constant $a$. The upper square gives $j_0g'=\overline g j_0'$. If $c_{h,k}:L(kh)^*\to Lh^*Lk^*$ denotes the cited composition isomorphism, then
$$\alpha=c_{j_0',\overline g}\circ c_{g',j_0}^{-1}:Lg'^*Lj_0^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lj_0'^*L\overline g^*.$$
This writes the two well-typed compositions explicitly and proves the claimed natural isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, second sentence: the pullback-composition isomorphism for the upper square

proof.text:
Write $J=j_{0!}$, $J'=j'_{0!}$, $H=Lg'^*$, $\overline H=L\overline g^*$, $G=Lg^*$, $P=Rp_*$, $P'=Rp'_*$, $Q=Rp^\times$, and $Q'=Rp'^\times$. The inverse mate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] specifies the open comparison on every object $K$ as
$$\gamma_K=\varepsilon^{J'}_{\overline HJK}\circ J'(\alpha_{JK})\circ J'H(\eta^J_K).$$
Consequently its mate is precisely $\alpha$, and the mate of $\delta_p:P'\overline H\to GP$ is $\beta_p:\overline HQ\to Q'G$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] with $(L_1,L_2,L_3,L_4)=(J,J',P,P')$, horizontal functors $(H,\overline H,G)$, and squares $(\gamma,\delta_p)$. The pasted square is exactly $\delta_f=(\delta_pJ)\circ(P'\gamma)$. Its mate for the composite adjunctions is therefore
$$\widetilde\beta_f=(Lj_0'^*\beta_p)\circ(\alpha Rp^\times):Lg'^*Lj_0^*Rp^\times\longrightarrow Lj_0'^*Rp'^\times Lg^*.$$
The unit/counit-preserving identifications of Step 1 identify this mate with the specified $\beta_f$; equivalently, clause (3) of the same pasting theorem gives the component equation
$$\rho'_{Lg^*L}\circ\beta_{f,L}=\widetilde\beta_{f,L}\circ Lg'^*(\rho_L)\qquad(L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)).$$
This is the required equality of the canonical comparison maps, not merely an isomorphism between their sources and targets.

source.place: Proof, second sentence: identification of the comparison for f with the pasted proper and open comparisons; explicit mate calculation

proof.text:
For every $L$, the displayed equation in Step 3 reads
$$\beta_{f,L}=(\rho'_{Lg^*L})^{-1}\circ Lj_0'^*(\beta_{p,L})\circ\alpha_{Rp^\times L}\circ Lg'^*(\rho_L).$$
The maps $\rho$, $\rho'$ and $\alpha$ are natural isomorphisms. The hypothesis makes $\beta_{p,L}$ invertible. A functor sends an inverse pair to an inverse pair, since $F(u)F(u^{-1})=F(1)=1$ and $F(u^{-1})F(u)=1$; thus the two whiskered maps are invertible. The inverse of the displayed composite is obtained by reversing the four factors and inverting each. Hence every component of $\beta_f$ is an isomorphism, as asserted.

source.place: Proof, final clause: conjugation and application of a functor preserve isomorphisms

Reuse the existing pro-etale derived pullback-composition theorem and Mathlib mate-pasting theorem; remove the new ill-typed duplicate node.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes both sentences of the blueprint proof: Step 1 factors compact support and identifies its right adjoints with compatible units/counits; Step 2 constructs the upper-square comparison by two applications of existing derived pullback composition; Step 3 expands the previously implicit mate-pasting argument; Step 4 proves invertibility. The imported unconditional ambient-datum claim is disputed in report.md.
